children: By Harry Robertson and Sophie  Kiderlin

Yields on French and Italian debt rose sharply on Wednesday as a global selloff driven by rising energy prices combined with concerns about high debt levels among some euro zone countries to shake bond markets.
German yields stayed broadly steady as investors sought safer assets, while those on short-dated debt fell as traders reduced their bets on European Central Bank rate hikes.
French 10-year yields (FR10YT=RR) surged as much as 18 basis points and were last up 12 bps at 4.87%, close to the 24-year high of 4.994% touched on Friday. Yields rise as prices fall and vice versa.

French bonds have been at the centre of the selloff in Europe as investors have worried about the country's wide budget deficit – which is more than 5% of GDP – and a divisive presidential election next year.

The gap between French and German 10-year yields (DE10FR10=RR), a proxy for the risk premium attached to France, rose 6 bps on Wednesday to 136 bps after hitting its highest since 2012 last week at almost 160 bps.
In recent days, the selling in French bond markets has reverberated across the euro zone, dragging down Italian and Greek debt as well as the euro
, which has fallen to a 17-month low.
Italy's 10-year bond yield
was last up 11 bps at 4.646%, not far from its highest since October 2023.
“OATs (French bonds) do have room to sell off further, but I don't necessarily mean that it's going to be a panic," said  Shriya Samarth, head of EMEA rates at StoneX.
“I would say so do US Treasuries; so do German bonds," she said, adding that inflation and fiscal risks were likely to keep yields high around the world.
GERMAN BONDS IN FAVOUR
German government debt found favour among investors, with the 10-year yield flat at 3.484% (DE10YT=RR).
Kenneth Broux, head of corporate research FX and rates at Societe Generale, said the moves indicated a preference for low-deficit, low-risk countries.
He added that the moves suggested that Tuesday's fall in yields was a reflection of investors reducing short positions.
"So we are not necessarily past the worst. I think that's the message that the market is really telling you," Broux said.
Short-dated bonds, which are sensitive to central bank rate expectations, outperformed longer-dated ones as traders trimmed bets on ECB tightening.
Germany's 2-year bond yield (DE2YT=RR) was last down 4 bps at 3.042%.
Traders were last pricing in around 55 bps of further ECB tightening by May next year, down from roughly 75 bps a week earlier.
Energy prices, inflation and interest rate concerns have put pressure on bonds globally in recent months, driving yields to multi-decade highs around the world.
The US 10-year yield
, the benchmark for borrowing costs around the world, rose to its highest since 2002 on Wednesday at 5.365%.
Brent crude oil futures
were up about 1% at $102 a barrel on Middle East supply risks and a storm heading for oil-producing regions in the United States.
France's finance minister said the country was considering issuing more shorter-term debt amid the turmoil in its longer-dated bonds.

France would be “strategic” in issuing new debt at a time when demand from investors has been hit by the country’s financial woes, finance minister Roland Lescure told the Wall Street Journal in an interview published Wednesday.
